title: Melbourne Shrubs & Climbers
description: Shrubs, climbers and scramblers seen across Greater Melbourne.
attribution: Species lists and photos: iNaturalist contributors (CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA). Text: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0).

cards.name: Hop Goodenia
cards.subtitle: Goodenia ovata
cards.description: Goodenia ovata, commonly called hop goodenia, is a species of flowering plant and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a shrub with sticky, often varnished foliage, toothed egg-shaped to elliptic leaves and racemes or thyrses of yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Goodenia ovata is an erect, ascending to prostrate shrub that typically grows to a height of 2 m (6 ft 7 in) and has sticky, often varnished foliage. The leaves are egg-shaped to elliptic, 30–80 mm (1.2–3.1 in) long and 10–40 mm (0.39–1.57 in) wide with toothed edges, on a petiole up to 30 mm (1.2 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: False Sarsaparilla
cards.subtitle: Hardenbergia violacea
cards.description: Hardenbergia violacea is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is known in Australia by the common names false sarsaparilla, purple coral pea, and waraburra. Elsewhere it is also called purple twining-pea, vine-lilac, and wild sarsaparilla.
cards.keyFeatures: Hardenbergia violacea is a prostrate or climbing sub-shrub with wiry stems up to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) or more long. The leaves are egg-shaped to lance-shaped, 30–100 mm (1.2–3.9 in) long and 10–50 mm (0.39–1.97 in) wide on a petiole about 10 mm (0.39 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Common Heath
cards.subtitle: Epacris impressa
cards.description: Epacris impressa, also known as common heath, is a species of plant in the heath family Ericaceae. It is native to south-eastern Australia (the states of Victoria, Tasmania, South Australia and New South Wales). French botanist Jacques Labillardière collected the species in 1793 and described it in 1805.
cards.keyFeatures: Epacris impressa grows as a woody shrub with an erect habit, sometimes reaching 2 to 3 m (6 ft 7 in to 9 ft 10 in) in height although plants in the range of 0.5 to 1 m (1 ft 8 in to 3 ft 3 in) tall are more commonly observed. The branches are stiff and have small leaves with prickly, pointed apices that are 8–16 mm (3⁄8–5⁄8 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Love Creeper
cards.subtitle: Comesperma volubile
cards.description: Comesperma volubile, commonly known as love creeper, is a slender climber in the family Polygalaceae. It is a twining plant with linear leaves and pea-like blue flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Comesperma voluble is a twining creeper to about 3 m (9.8 ft) high on rare occasion a small shrublet with smooth, angled stems. There are few leaves, linear to oval-shaped, 10–45 mm (0.39–1.77 in) long, 1.5–9 mm (0.059–0.354 in) wide, lower surface pale, margins curved or rolled under.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Prickly Currant-Bush
cards.subtitle: Coprosma quadrifida
cards.description: Coprosma quadrifida is a dioecious shrub of the family Rubiaceae native to southeastern Australia. First described as Canthium quadrifidum by Labillardiere, it was given its current name by B. L.
cards.keyFeatures: These plants are an erect open to dense shrub that can grow to between 2-5m tall. Seed germination can take over six months, with domestically used seed undergoing stratification to reduce germination to 2–4 weeks.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rolf Lawrenz, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Rolf Lawrenz

cards.name: Wonga Vine
cards.subtitle: Pandorea pandorana
cards.description: Pandorea pandorana, commonly known as the wonga wonga vine or wonga-vine, is a species of flowering plant in the family Bignoniaceae and is native to Australia, Malesia and the southwestern Pacific region. It is a woody scrambler or climber with pinnate leaves, juvenile leaves differing from those of mature plants.
cards.keyFeatures: Pandorea pandorana is a glabrous woody climber or scrambler, sometimes reaching a height of 6 m (20 ft) or more. The leaves are arranged in opposite pairs and pinnate, those of juvenile plants 20–80 mm (0.79–3.15 in) long with eight to seventeen wavy-edged leaflets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tim, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Tim

cards.name: Grey Parrot Pea
cards.subtitle: Dillwynia cinerascens
cards.description: Dillwynia cinerascens, commonly known as grey parrot-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect to low-lying shrub with linear or thread-like leaves and orange or yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Dillwynia cinerascens is a low-lying to erect, heath-like shrub that grows to a height of 0.3–1.5 m (1 ft 0 in – 4 ft 11 in) with hairs flattened against its stems. The leaves are linear to thread-like, 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) long and 0.3–0.5 mm (0.012–0.020 in) wide, sometimes with a few white hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Cathy Powers, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Cathy Powers

cards.name: Button Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Coronidium scorpioides
cards.description: Coronidium scorpioides, commonly known as button everlasting, is a perennial, herbaceous shrub in the family Asteraceae and is found in eastern Australia. It has sessile, egg-shaped to lance-shaped leaves, solitary heads of usually pale or lemon-yellow flowers and narrowly cylindrical achenes. It was previously known as Helichrysum scorpioides.
cards.keyFeatures: Button everlasting is an ascending to erect, herbaceous perennial plant that typically grows to 5–55 cm (2.0–21.7 in) high with simple stems or few branches usually from arising from a rosette.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Round-leaf Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia acinacea
cards.description: Acacia acinacea, commonly known as gold dust wattle, wreath wattle or round-leaf wattle. is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia acinacea is a bushy or straggling, open shrub that typically grows to a height of around 2.5 m (8 ft 2 in). Its phyllodes are asymmetric, narrowly oblong to lance-shaped or egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, 4–15 mm (0.16–0.59 in) long and 2 to 8 mm (0.079 to 0.315 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: Australian Indigo
cards.subtitle: Indigofera australis
cards.description: Indigofera australis commonly known as Australian indigo, Austral indigo, native indigo or hill indigo, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is an erect, spreading shrub with pinnate leaves, pink to purple flowers and terete pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Indigofera australis is an erect, spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 2.5 m (8 ft 2 in) high and wide, with arching branches and flexible stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Greg Tasney, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Greg Tasney

cards.name: Common Correa
cards.subtitle: Correa reflexa
cards.description: Correa reflexa, commonly known as common correa or native fuchsia, is a shrub which is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants are quite variable and a large number of varieties and local forms have been identified. Heights vary from prostrate to 1.5 metres high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Eamonn Culhane, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Eamonn Culhane

cards.name: Australian Dusty Miller
cards.subtitle: Spyridium parvifolium
cards.description: Spyridium parvifolium, commonly known dusty miller, is a flowering plant in the family Rhamnaceae. It has dark green leaves and clusters of small, whitish flowers at the end of branches. It is widespread in eastern states of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Spyridium parvifolium is a low, spreading shrub to about 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) high with smaller branches thickly covered in soft, long, rusty coloured hairs. The dull green leaves are obovate, elliptic or orb shaped, 4–18 mm (0.16–0.71 in) long, 3–13 mm (0.12–0.51 in) wide, and the apex rounded or notched.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Common Beard-heath
cards.subtitle: Leucopogon virgatus
cards.description: Leucopogon virgatus, commonly known as common beard-heath, is a species of flowering plant in the heath family Ericaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect to low-lying shrub with linear to narrowly lance-shaped or egg-shaped leaves, and erect clusters of three to seven white, tube-shaped flowers on the ends of branches and in upper leaf axils.
cards.keyFeatures: Leucopogon virgatus is an erect to low-lying shrub that typically grows to a height of 35–60 cm (14–24 in) high and has softly-hairy, redish brown branchlets. The leaves are more or less erect, linear to narrowly lance-shaped or egg-shaped, 2–25 mm (0.079–0.984 in) long and 0.9–5.0 mm (0.035–0.197 in) wide on a petiole up to 1 mm (0.039 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Australian Clematis
cards.subtitle: Clematis aristata
cards.description: Clematis aristata, known as Australian clematis, wild clematis, goat's beard or old man's beard, is a climbing shrub of the family Ranunculaceae, found in eastern Australia in dry and wet forests of Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Native Raspberry
cards.subtitle: Rubus parvifolius
cards.description: Rubus parvifolius is a species of bramble native to Asia and Australia. It is commonly called Japanese bramble, Australian raspberry (in the United States), and native raspberry (in Australia).
cards.keyFeatures: Rubus parvifolius is a scrambling shrub up to 2 metres (6+1⁄2 feet) tall. The arching branches are armed with curved prickles.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Allen

cards.name: Early Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia genistifolia
cards.description: Acacia genistifolia commonly known as spreading wattle or early wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an open, erect, straggly or spreading shrub with sessile, more or less rigid, sharply pointed phyllodes, spherical heads of cream-coloured to rich lemon yellow flowers, and linear, thinly leathery pods raised over the seeds.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia genistifolia is an open, erect, straggly or spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.6–3 m (2 ft 0 in – 9 ft 10 in) high and has ribbed branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Quentin Groom

cards.name: Running Postman
cards.subtitle: Kennedia prostrata
cards.description: Kennedia prostrata, commonly known as running postman, scarlet coral pea or scarlet runner, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a prostrate or twining shrub with trifoliate leaves and, usually, red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Kennedia prostrata is a prostrate or twining shrub with wiry stems up to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) long that are hairy when young. The leaves are on a petiole vary from 5 to 50 mm (0.20 to 1.97 in) long, with more or less round leaflets, which are from 6 to 35 mm (0.24 to 1.38 in) long and wide with wavy edges.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by insiderelic

cards.name: Common Flat-pea
cards.subtitle: Platylobium obtusangulum
cards.description: Platylobium obtusangulum, the common flat-pea, is a shrub that is endemic to Australia. It is a member of the family Fabaceae and of the genus Platylobium. The species is an erect or straggling shrub that can grow up to 1 metre in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Rod Lowther, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Kangaroo-apple
cards.subtitle: Solanum laciniatum
cards.description: Solanum laciniatum (also known as poroporo or bullibulli) a soft-wooded shrub native to the east coast of Australia, notably Victoria and Tasmania. It also occurs in Western Australia and New Zealand, where some authorities consider it to be introduced. It is similar to Solanum aviculare, with which it shares the common name kangaroo apple.
cards.keyFeatures: The shrub typically grows to a height and width of 1 to 3 m (3 ft 3 in to 9 ft 10 in) and blooms between January and February, producing purple blue flowers. Solanum laciniatum is a hardy and short-lived glabrous perennial plant which can reach between 1 and 3 metres in height, but occasionally can reach up to 4 metres.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Murray NZ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Murray NZ

cards.name: Creeping Bossiaea
cards.subtitle: Bossiaea prostrata
cards.description: Bossiaea prostrata, commonly known as creeping bossiaea, is a prostrate understory shrub in the pea family, Fabaceae. It is a widespread species with orange-yellow flowers, purple-brown keels and trailing branches.
cards.keyFeatures: Bossiaea prostrata is a shrub with a prostrate spreading, scrambling habit to 0.2 m (7.9 in) wide. The leaves are dark green on the upper side and paler on the underside, ovate to rounded or oblong, 3–15 mm (0.12–0.59 in) long, 2–10 mm (0.079–0.394 in) wide and have a petiole about 5 mm (0.20 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Thomas Nataprawira, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Thomas Nataprawira

cards.name: Clustered Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Chrysocephalum semipapposum
cards.description: Chrysocephalum semipapposum, commonly known as clustered everlasting is a perennial shrub native to Australia. Clustered everlasting belongs to the family Asteraceae. C. semipapposum produces terminal flowers heads in clusters, mainly between spring and early summer with silver-grey appearing stems and branches.
cards.keyFeatures: Chrysocephalum semipapposum is a perennial herbaceous shrub, which is highly variable. Generally, the erect shrub is 15–60 cm high, and is sprawling in nature, with its width up to 40 cm.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bridal Creeper
cards.subtitle: Asparagus asparagoides
cards.description: Asparagus asparagoides, commonly known as bridal creeper, bridal-veil creeper, gnarboola, smilax or smilax asparagus, is a herbaceous climbing plant of the family Asparagaceae native to eastern and southern Africa. Sometimes grown as an ornamental plant, it has become a serious environmental weed in Australia and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Asparagus asparagoides grows as a herbaceous vine with a scrambling or climbing habit which can reach 3 m (10 ft) in length. It has shiny green leaf-like structures (cladodes) which are flattened stems rather than true leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Hibbard, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by John Hibbard

cards.name: Golden Bush-pea
cards.subtitle: Pultenaea gunnii
cards.description: Pultenaea gunnii, commonly known as golden bush-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a slender, erect to spreading shrub with hairy young stems, egg-shaped to lance-shaped leaves with lance-shaped stipules at the base, and bright yellow and dark red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pultenaea graveolens is a slender, erect to spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) and stems that are sparsely hairy when young.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Black Nightshade
cards.subtitle: Solanum nigrum
cards.description: Solanum nigrum, the European black nightshade or simply black nightshade or blackberry nightshade, is a species of flowering plant in the family Solanaceae, native to Eurasia and introduced in the Americas, Australasia, and South Africa. Ripe berries and cooked leaves of edible strains are used as food in some locales, and plant parts are used as a traditional medicine.
cards.keyFeatures: Black nightshade is a common herb or short-lived perennial shrub, found in many wooded areas, as well as disturbed habitats.
cards.imageCredit: (c) jamie-aa, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by jamie-aa

cards.name: Wedding Bush
cards.subtitle: Ricinocarpos pinifolius
cards.description: Ricinocarpos pinifolius, commonly known as wedding bush, is a shrub of the family Euphorbiaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It has fragrant daisy-like flowers in spring.
cards.keyFeatures: Ricinocarpos pinifolius is a small shrub 1–3 m (3 ft 3 in – 9 ft 10 in) high and 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) wide with smooth branches. The smooth leaves are narrow, 1–3 mm (0.039–0.118 in) wide, 1–4 cm (0.39–1.57 in) long and the leaf margin may be either rolled downwards or backwards on a petiole about 3 mm (0.12 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Steve Llewellyn, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Myrtle Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia myrtifolia
cards.description: Acacia myrtifolia, known colloquially as myrtle wattle, red stem wattle, red-stemmed wattle or South Australian silver wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae, and is endemic to coastal or near-coastal areas of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia myrtifolia is a glabrous, bushy shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.5–3 m (1 ft 8 in – 9 ft 10 in) and 2–3 m (6 ft 7 in – 9 ft 10 in) with smooth grey bark, often red new shoots and angled, prominently ribbed, normally red branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) guymer, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Honey-pots
cards.subtitle: Acrotriche serrulata
cards.description: Acrotriche serrulata, commonly known as honey pots, is a species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae, and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a low-lying, mat-forming shrub with lance-shaped to linear leaves, pale green to whitish, cylindrical flowers and greyish-green fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Acrotriche serrulata is a low-lying, matt-forming shrub that typically spreads to about 1 m (3 ft 3 in) wide, with ascending branches up to 15–60 cm (5.9–23.6 in) high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Musk Daisy-bush
cards.subtitle: Olearia argophylla
cards.description: Shawia argophylla, commonly known as musk daisy-bush, native musk or silver shrub, is a species of flowering plant in the family Asteraceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a shrub or tree with silvery branchlets, egg-shaped to elliptic leaves, and white and yellow, daisy-like inflorescences.
cards.keyFeatures: Shawia argophylla is a shrub or tree that typically grows to a height of up to about 10 m (33 ft), and has fissured to slightly stringy or flaky bark. Its branchlets are densely covered with fine, silvery or pale brown hairs pressed against the surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Montpellier Broom
cards.subtitle: Genista monspessulana
cards.description: Genista monspessulana, commonly known as French broom, Montpellier broom, or Cape broom (Australia), is a woody leguminous perennial shrub. The yellow-flowering bush is native to the Mediterranean region, and while it may still be commonly sold in some garden stores, it is considered an invasive plant in most places where it has been introduced.
cards.keyFeatures: G. monspessulana grows to 1–2.5 metres (3+1⁄2–8 feet) tall, with slender green branches. Stems generally ridged or angled and green when young.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Philipp Weigell, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Pink-bells
cards.subtitle: Tetratheca ciliata
cards.description: Tetratheca ciliata, commonly known as pink bells, is a small shrub in the family Elaeocarpaceae. It is endemic to southern Australia. It is a small shrub which may grow up to 100 cm high.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kevin Sparrow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kevin Sparrow

cards.name: Yellow Rice-flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea flava
cards.description: Pimelea flava is a species of flowering plant in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a shrub with narrowly elliptic to egg-shaped leaves arranged in opposite pairs, and compact clusters of 9 or more flowers with 2 or 4 elliptic to circular involucral bracts at the base. The flowers and bracts are white or yellow, depending on subspecies.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea flava is a shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.3–2.5 m (1 ft 0 in – 8 ft 2 in) and has hairy young stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Peter Crowcroft

cards.name: Twining Glycine
cards.subtitle: Glycine clandestina
cards.description: Glycine clandestina commonly known as twining glycine, is a flowering plant in the family Fabaceae. It has green leaves with three leaflets, mauve pea flowers and grows in Tasmania and eastern states of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Glycine clandestina is a slender, twining climber, stems up to 50 cm (20 in) long covered in soft hairs, winding over grasses and taller shrubs. Leaves consist of three, variable sized, linear-shaped leaflets, 12–50 mm (0.47–1.97 in) long, 2–8 mm (0.079–0.315 in) wide and occasional appressed hairs, apex rounded or pointed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Clarke, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Ruby Saltbush
cards.subtitle: Enchylaena tomentosa
cards.description: Enchylaena tomentosa commonly known as barrier saltbush or ruby saltbush,is a flowering plant in the family Amaranthaceae. It is a small shrub with greyish soft leaves, small flowers and fleshy berries.
cards.keyFeatures: Enchylaena tomentosa grows as a small perennial shrub, up to a meter in diameter. Leaves are slender and cylindrical growing to 6-15mm long, both leaves and stems are densely covered in woolly hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Rosemary Grevillea
cards.subtitle: Grevillea rosmarinifolia
cards.description: Grevillea rosmarinifolia, commonly known as rosemary grevillea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Proteaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia and naturalised in other parts of the country. It is usually an erect, compact to open shrub with linear, narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblong leaves with the edges rolled under, and loose clusters of pink to red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Grevillea rosmarinifolia is usually an erect, compact to open, sometimes low shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.3–2 m (1 ft 0 in – 6 ft 7 in). Its leaves are linear to narrowly elliptic or narrowly oblong, 8–38 mm (0.31–1.50 in) long and 0.7–3 mm (0.028–0.118 in) wide with the edges rolled under, usually concealing the lower surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Grey Mistletoe
cards.subtitle: Amyema quandang
cards.description: Amyema quandang is a species of hemi-parasitic shrub which is widespread throughout the mainland of Australia, especially arid inland regions, sometimes referred to as the grey mistletoe.
cards.keyFeatures: An aerial shrub, without conventional roots, which attaches to the stems of species of Acacia. The leaves are leathery and greyish, and lanceolate to broadly ovate.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jean-Paul Boerekamps

cards.name: Tutsan
cards.subtitle: Hypericum androsaemum
cards.description: Hypericum androsaemum, the shrubby St. John's wort, is a species of flowering plant in the family Hypericaceae. It is commonly called tutsan or sweet-amber.
cards.keyFeatures: Hypericum androsaemum is a small bushy shrub, reaching 30–70 centimetres (12–28 in) tall. It has many stems which remain upright and erect instead of creeping over the ground.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Showy Bossiaea
cards.subtitle: Bossiaea cinerea
cards.description: Bossiaea cinerea, commonly known as showy bossiaea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub with trowel-shaped, triangular, egg-shaped or lance-shaped leaves with a sharply-pointed tip and golden yellow and red to purplish-brown flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Bossiaea cinerea is an erect to spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) tall and has densely hairy stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Richard Dimon, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Richard Dimon

cards.name: Grey Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Ozothamnus obcordatus
cards.description: Ozothamnus obcordatus, the grey everlasting, is a shrub in the family Asteraceae, native to the states of Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania in Australia. It grows to 1.5 metres high and has obcordate, broad-elliptic obovate leaves which are 6 to 15 mm long and 3 to 6 mm wide. These have tips that bend backwards and are shiny and green on the top and covered with grey hairs underneath.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Tough Rice-flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea axiflora
cards.description: Pimelea axiflora, commonly known as bootlace bush, is a small shrub in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a small shrub with whitish flowers on mostly smooth stems.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea axiflora is a small dioecious shrub 0.2–3 m (8 in – 9 ft 10 in) high with smooth stems or occasionally hairy. The leaves are arranged in opposite pairs are mostly linear or narrowly elliptic, upper surface mid-green, underside paler, 5–60 mm (0.20–2.36 in) long, 2–10 mm (0.079–0.394 in) wide on a petiole 3 mm (0.12 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ian Rainbow, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ian Rainbow

cards.name: Gorse
cards.subtitle: Ulex europaeus
cards.description: Ulex europaeus, commonly known as gorse, common gorse, furze or whin, is a species of flowering plant native to Western Europe.
cards.keyFeatures: Growing to 4.5 metres (10 ft) tall, it is an evergreen shrub. The young stems are green, with the shoots and leaves modified into green spines, 1–3 centimetres (1⁄2–1+1⁄4 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) lejones417, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Grey Saltbush
cards.subtitle: Atriplex cinerea
cards.description: Atriplex cinerea, commonly known as grey saltbush, coast saltbush, barilla or truganini, is a plant species in the family Amaranthaceae. It occurs in sheltered coastal areas and around salt lakes in the Australian states of Western Australia, South Australia, Tasmania, Victoria and New South Wales.
cards.keyFeatures: Atriplex cinerea is a prostrate to erect, heavily branched, leafy shrub growing up to 1.8m high and up to 2.5 m wide. Stems are initially ridged and angular, becoming woody with age.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tony Rebelo, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tony Rebelo

cards.name: Rock Correa
cards.subtitle: Correa glabra
cards.description: Correa glabra, commonly known as the rock correa, is a species of tall, erect shrub that is endemic to Australia. It usually has elliptical, mostly glabrous leaves and pendent, pale green to pale yellow flowers arranged singly on short side shoots.
cards.keyFeatures: Correa glabra is an erect shrub that typically grows to a height of 2.7 m (8 ft 10 in). The leaves are elliptical to sometimes egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, papery to leathery, 10–40 mm (0.39–1.57 in) long and 5–17 mm (0.20–0.67 in) wide with a strong, sweet lemon scent when crushed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Seaberry Saltbush
cards.subtitle: Rhagodia candolleana
cards.description: Chenopodium candolleanum (Syn. Rhagodia candolleana), commonly known as seaberry saltbush, is a shrub in the subfamily Chenopodioideae of the family Amaranthaceae (sensu lato), native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: This species forms a dense shrub up to 2 metres in height. It shiny green leaves are thick and almost succulent, with a paler underside.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Terra Occ

cards.name: Needle-leaved Broom
cards.subtitle: Genista linifolia
cards.description: Genista linifolia is a species of broom known by the common names Mediterranean broom, needle-leaved broom and flax broom. It is native to southwestern Europe, North Africa, and the Canary Islands.
cards.keyFeatures: This is a shrub with hairy green stems and branches which can exceed two meters in height. Its leaves are made up of tough, green, lance-shaped leaflets with woolly undersides.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacob Moore, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Hemp Bush
cards.subtitle: Gynatrix pulchella
cards.description: Gynatrix pulchella, known commonly as the hemp bush or Aboriginal hemp, is a flowering shrub in the family Malvaceae that is endemic to southeast Australia
cards.keyFeatures: It can grow as a shrub or tree to a height of 5 metres, although it has a mean height of 3 metres. Plants of this species have a bushy, erect or spreading growth habit and reach reproductive maturity in 1 to 5 years.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: White Elderberry
cards.subtitle: Sambucus gaudichaudiana
cards.description: Sambucus gaudichaudiana, commonly known as white elderberry, is a species of flowering plant in the family Viburnaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is a perennial shrub but with stems that are produced annually with pinnate leaves that have three to eleven leaflets, small white flowers and small but edible fruit. It grows in cool forest and shady gorges.
cards.keyFeatures: Sambucus gaudichaudiana is a shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) from a perennial rootstock but with grooved stems that are renewed each year.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lek Khauv, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: African Boxthorn
cards.subtitle: Lycium ferocissimum
cards.description: Lycium ferocissimum is a species of flowering plants in the nightshade family, Solanaceae. It is sometimes referred to by the common names African boxthorn, boxthorn, and snake-berry. This shrub is native to Cape Provinces, Free State, and Lesotho.
cards.keyFeatures: African boxthorn is a large shrub which grows up to 5 metres (16 ft) high and is covered in spines. The spines are of randomly varying lengths along the branch and, unlike most other species of Lycium (except for Lycium amoenum), they take the form of stout "peg-thorns".
cards.imageCredit: (c) Daniel Cahen, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Daniel Cahen

cards.name: Creeping Mistletoe
cards.subtitle: Muellerina eucalyptoides
cards.description: Muellerina eucalyptoides, commonly known as creeping mistletoe, is a hemiparasitic aerial shrub in the family Loranthaceae. The species is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: M. eucalyptoides is pendulous in habit, unlike other Muellerina species, but has the long epicortical runners of all Muellerina species. The leaves are opposite with indistinct venation.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Josh, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Cranberry Heath
cards.subtitle: Styphelia humifusa
cards.description: Styphelia humifusa, commonly known as native cranberry or cranberry heath, is a small prostrate shrub or groundcover in the heath family Ericaceae. The species is endemic to south-eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Styphelia humifusa grows as a spreading mat-like shrub up to 50 cm (20 in) high and 0.5 to 1.5 m (20 in to 5 ft) across. Its hairy stems bear blue-green pine-like acute leaves 0.5-1.2 cm (0.2-0.5 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Spanish Heath
cards.subtitle: Erica lusitanica
cards.description: Erica lusitanica is a European species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae, known by the common names Portuguese heath and Spanish heath.
cards.keyFeatures: Erica lusitanica is a hairy, woody shrub just under 2 metres (6+1⁄2 feet) in maximum height. It is densely covered in plumes of green, leathery, needle-like evergreen leaves each less than a centimeter long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacqui Geux, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacqui Geux

cards.name: Rough Bush-pea
cards.subtitle: Pultenaea scabra
cards.description: Pultenaea scabra, commonly known as rough bush-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub with hairy stems, heart-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, and yellow and red, pea-like flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pultenaea scabra is an erect or spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–3 m (3 ft 3 in – 9 ft 10 in) and has densely hairy stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Showy Parrot-pea
cards.subtitle: Dillwynia sericea
cards.description: Dillwynia sericea, commonly known as showy parrot-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect to low-lying shrub with hairy stems, linear leaves and apricot-coloured flowers, usually with a red centre.
cards.keyFeatures: Dillwynia sericea is an erect, to low-lying, heath-like shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.5–1 m (1 ft 8 in – 3 ft 3 in) with stiff branches that are hairy, especially when young. The leaves are linear, mostly 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) long and less than 1 mm (0.039 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: White Correa
cards.subtitle: Correa alba
cards.description: Correa alba, commonly known as white correa, is a species of shrub that is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It has egg-shaped to more or less circular leaves, erect white flowers arranged singly or in groups on short side branches, and green fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Correa alba is a prostrate to spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) and has rust-coloured, woolly-hairy young stems. The leaves are leathery, elliptic to more or less round, 8–35 mm (0.31–1.38 in) long and 6–25 mm (0.24–0.98 in) wide on a petiole 0.5–1.5 mm (0.020–0.059 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Jesse Rorabaugh

cards.name: Cape-ivy
cards.subtitle: Delairea odorata
cards.description: Delairea odorata is a climber within the family Asteraceae that is native to South Africa. One of the two species in the genus Delairea (the other being Delairea aparadensis), it was previously included in the genus Senecio as Senecio mikanioides. It is known as Cape ivy in some parts of the world (US) and German ivy in others (Britain, Ireland).
cards.keyFeatures: Delairea odorata is a fast-growing vine that can climb to heights of 2–4 metres (7–13 ft). The glossy and semi-succulent leaves, which are 3–10 centimetres (1+1⁄4–4 in) long and 3–8 centimetres (1+1⁄4–3+1⁄4 in) wide, are alternately arranged along the stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Ken-ichi Ueda, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Ken-ichi Ueda

cards.name: Sticky Boobialla
cards.subtitle: Myoporum petiolatum
cards.description: Myoporum petiolatum, commonly known as sticky boobialla, is a plant in the figwort family Scrophulariaceae, and is endemic to the south-east of continental Australia. For many years this species has been confused with the much less common species Myoporum viscosum from which it can be distinguished by its thinner, noticeably petiolate and non-odorous leaves.
cards.keyFeatures: Myoporum petiolatum is a shrub which usually grows to between 0.5 and 2.0 metres (2 and 7 ft) in height. Its leaves are arranged alternately and have a distinct petiole 5–13 millimetres (0.2–0.5 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Common Aotus
cards.subtitle: Aotus ericoides
cards.description: Aotus ericoides, also known as common aotus or golden pea, is a shrub in the family Fabaceae. It flowers in leaf axils in spring and has yellow pea flowers with splotches of red. It is endemic to eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Aotus ericoides is a variable shrub that may grow up to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) high. The stems are often covered in short, matted, rusty or greyish coloured hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lorraine Phelan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lorraine Phelan

cards.name: Sweet Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia suaveolens
cards.description: Acacia suaveolens (sweet wattle) is a shrub species endemic to Australia. It grows to between 0.3 and 3.5 metres high and has smooth purplish-brown or light green bark and has straight or slightly curving blue-green phyllodes. The pale yellow to near white globular flower heads generally appear between April and September in its native range.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lewis, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Lewis

cards.name: Hop Bitter-pea
cards.subtitle: Daviesia latifolia
cards.description: Daviesia latifolia, commonly known as hop bitter-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a slender, erect, spreading shrub with elliptic, egg-shaped or lance-shaped phyllodes and orange-yellow and maroon flowers in long racemes.
cards.keyFeatures: Daviesia latifolia is a slender, erect shrub that typically grows to 1–5 m (3 ft 3 in – 16 ft 5 in) high and 1.0–1.5 m (3 ft 3 in – 4 ft 11 in) wide and has arching, glabrous branches. Adult phyllodes are elliptic to egg-shaped or lance-shaped, 20–150 mm (0.79–5.91 in) long and 5–70 mm (0.20–2.76 in) wide on a petiole-like base 3–20 mm (0.12–0.79 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved

cards.name: Cock's-eggs
cards.subtitle: Salpichroa origanifolia
cards.description: Salpichroa origanifolia is a species of flowering plant in the nightshade family known by the common names lily of the valley vine, pampas lily-of-the-valley or cock's-eggs.
cards.keyFeatures: Salpichroa origanifolia can reach a stem length of about 2–3 m (6 ft 7 in – 9 ft 10 in). This perennial, rhizomatous, decumbent to climbing, hairy vine has a trailing, highly branched, four-cornered zig-zagging stems.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Julien Renoult, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Julien Renoult

cards.name: Spike Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia oxycedrus
cards.description: Acacia oxycedrus, commonly known as spike wattle, is an erect or spreading shrub which is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The prickly shrub grows to a height of 1 to 3 m (3 ft 3 in to 9 ft 10 in) and has a width of around 2 m (6 ft 7 in)with a dense habit. Like most species of Acacia it has phyllodes rather than true leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petra Holland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petra Holland

cards.name: Curved Rice-flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea curviflora
cards.description: Pimelea curviflora, also known as curved rice-flower, is a shrub in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to Australia. It is a small, hairy shrub with greenish-yellow or red tubular flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea curviflora is a small understory woody shrub 20–150 cm (7.9–59.1 in) high with soft hairy stems. The yellowish-green leaves are elliptic, lance or egg-shaped 5–20 mm (0.20–0.79 in) long, 2–8 mm (0.079–0.315 in) wide and hairy on both sides.
cards.imageCredit: (c) yatesy, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by yatesy

cards.name: Furze Hakea
cards.subtitle: Hakea ulicina
cards.description: Hakea ulicina, commonly known as furze hakea, is a shrub in the family Proteaceae and endemic to Victoria, Australia. It has stiff, long, narrow leaves and creamy-white flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Hakea ulicina is an erect shrub or small tree growing between 2–5 m (7–20 ft) tall, resprouting from a lignotuber. The leaves are mostly linear, curving, rigid, 3–18 cm (1–7 in) long and 1–4 mm (0.04–0.2 in) wide with 1-3 prominent longitudinal veins on the upper and lower surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Kangaroo Apple
cards.subtitle: Solanum aviculare
cards.description: Solanum aviculare, commonly known as kangaroo apple or New Zealand nightshade, is a species of flowering plant in the family Solanaceae and native to New Zealand and the east coast of Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Solanum aviculare is an erect shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 4 m (13 ft) tall.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Peter de Lange

cards.name: Common Wedge-pea
cards.subtitle: Gompholobium huegelii
cards.description: Gompholobium huegelii, commonly known as common wedge-pea is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub with trifoliate leaves and cream-coloured to yellow and greenish, pea-like flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Gompholobium huegelii is an erect or spreading, more or less glabrous shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Lorraine Phelan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Lorraine Phelan

cards.name: Heath Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia brownii
cards.description: Acacia brownii, commonly known as heath wattle or prickly Moses, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to eastern continental Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub with more or less rigid, straight, sharply-pointed phyllodes, bright yellow flowers arranged in spherical heads and curved, flat, leathery pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia brownii is an erect or spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.3 to 1 m (1 ft 0 in to 3 ft 3 in) and has glabrous to sparsely hairy branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Yellow Hakea
cards.subtitle: Hakea nodosa
cards.description: Hakea nodosa, commonly known as yellow hakea, is a shrub that is endemic to Australia. It usually has golden yellow flowers in profusion and needle-shaped leaves.
cards.keyFeatures: Hakea nodosa is an erect, sprawling shrub usually growing to 3 m (9.8 ft) tall and a similar width. The branchlets quickly form ribbing or slowly becoming smooth.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Austral Bear’s-ears
cards.subtitle: Cymbonotus preissianus
cards.description: Cymbonotus preissianus, commonly known as Austral bears ear, is an Australian species of small shrub in the family Asteraceae. A perennial herbaceous plant without stems, to 30 cm in diameter. Yellow flowers form from August to March.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Donald Hobern, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Silver Cassia
cards.subtitle: Senna artemisioides
cards.description: Senna artemisioides, commonly known as silver cassia, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to Australia, where it is found in all mainland states and territories. It is a shrub with pinnate leaves, the leaflets variable, yellow flowers mostly occurring in winter, and linear pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Senna artemisioides is a shrub that typically grows to a height of.15–3 m (5.9 in – 9 ft 10.1 in) high and has pinnate leaves, the leaflets in pairs of one to eight, with a sessile gland between the lowest pair of leaflets. The leaves have tiny, triangular stipules, but fall off as the leaves mature.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Victor Phillips, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Tangled Lignum
cards.subtitle: Duma florulenta
cards.description: Duma florulenta (synonym Muehlenbeckia florulenta), commonly known as tangled lignum or often simply lignum, is a plant native to inland Australia. It is associated with wetland habitats, especially those in arid and semiarid regions subject to cycles of intermittent flooding and drying out. The Wiradjuri name for the plant is gweeargal, and the Walmajarri name is Kirinykiriny, or Kurinykuriny.
cards.keyFeatures: Lignum is a perennial, dioecious shrub, growing to 2.5 m in height, with its multitude of thin, intertwined and tangled branches and branchlets forming dense thickets to the exclusion of other species. Its thin, narrow leaves are 15–70 mm long and 2–10 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by insiderelic

cards.name: Juniper Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia ulicifolia
cards.description: Acacia ulicifolia, commonly known as prickly Moses or juniper wattle is a shrub of the genus Acacia and the subgenus Phyllodineae, native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia ulicifolia is decumbent to an erect shrub 0.5–2 m (1 ft 8 in – 6 ft 7 in) high, with smooth grey bark. The phyllodes which are leaf like in appearance and function, are short and needle like, 8–14 mm (0.31–0.55 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Terra Occ, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Matted Bush-pea
cards.subtitle: Pultenaea pedunculata
cards.description: Pultenaea pedunculata, commonly known as matted bush-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a prostrate, densely matted shrub with softly-hairy branches that often form roots, narrow elliptic leaves, and bright yellow and brick-red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pultenaea peduncluata is a prostrate, densely-matted shrub that forms carpets of 1 m (3 ft 3 in) or more in diameter, and has softy-hairy branches. The branches are up to several metres long but rarely more than 20 cm (7.9 in) off the ground, and often from roots to it.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Elspeth Swan

cards.name: Smooth Parrot-pea
cards.subtitle: Dillwynia glaberrima
cards.description: Dillwynia glaberrima commonly known as the smooth parrot-pea, is an Australian flowering plant in the family Fabaceae. It is a small upright shrub with linear leaves and clusters of yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: This species is a spreading or erect shrub to 2 metres in height with cylindrical leaves to 2.5 cm long, with a short, often recurved apex. The bright yellow pea flowers have red markings and are proportionately quite wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Cowirrie

cards.name: Native Broom
cards.subtitle: Viminaria juncea
cards.description: Viminaria juncea is the single species in the genus Viminaria endemic to Australia. The genus is in the pea family Fabaceae. It is colloquially known as native broom after its resemblance to the related European broom plants.
cards.keyFeatures: Native broom grows as an erect or weeping shrub 1.5–6 m (4.9–19.7 ft) high and 1–2.5 m (3.3–8.2 ft) wide. It has a smooth trunk and ascending branches while the minor branchlets often droop.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Joe Atkinson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Joe Atkinson

cards.name: Bundled Hibbertia
cards.subtitle: Hibbertia fasciculata
cards.description: Hibbertia fasciculata is a species of flowering plant in the family Dilleniaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a small erect to spreading shrub with glabrous stems except on new growth, narrow linear leaves, and yellow flowers arranged in leaf axils, with eight to twelve stamens surrounding three carpels.
cards.keyFeatures: Hibbertia fasciculata is an erect or sprawling shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 40 cm (16 in) with glabrous branches except on the new growth. The leaves are clustered, narrow linear, 4–6 mm (0.16–0.24 in) long and up to 0.5 mm (0.020 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) T. Hammer, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Small-leaf Parrot-pea
cards.subtitle: Dillwynia phylicoides
cards.description: Dillwynia phylicoides, commonly known as small-leaf parrot-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is an erect to open shrub with twisted, linear to narrow oblong leaves, and yellow and red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Dillwynia phylicoides is an erect to open shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1.5 m (4 ft 11 in) and has stiff, spreading hairs on the stems. The leaves are twisted, linear to narrow oblong, 3–8 mm (0.12–0.31 in) long, about 0.5 mm (0.020 in) wide on a petiole 0.2–0.5 mm (0.0079–0.0197 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Coarse Dodder-laurel
cards.subtitle: Cassytha melantha
cards.description: Cassytha melantha is a parasitic vine. Common names include coarse dodder-laurel and large dodder-laurel. The fruits are about 10–15 millimetres (0.39–0.59 in) in diameter and are green, drying to black.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Chris Lindorff, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Chris Lindorff

cards.name: Large-leaf Bush Pea
cards.subtitle: Pultenaea daphnoides
cards.description: Pultenaea daphnoides, commonly known as large-leaf bush-pea or large-leaf bitter-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect shrub with egg-shaped to wedge-shaped leaves with a pointed tip, and dense clusters of bright yellow and red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pultenaea daphnoides is an erect shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–3 m (3 ft 3 in – 9 ft 10 in) and has hairy, four-angled stems. The leaves are wedge-shaped to egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, 5–40 mm (0.20–1.57 in) long and 2–11 mm (0.079–0.433 in) wide with a pointed tip and stipules 1–2 mm (0.039–0.079 in) long at the base.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Melburnian, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Dolichos Pea
cards.subtitle: Dipogon lignosus
cards.description: Dipogon lignosus, the okie bean, Cape sweet-pea, dolichos pea or mile-a-minute vine, is a species of flowering plant in the legume family, Fabaceae. It is the only species classified in the monotypic genus Dipogon which belongs to the subfamily Faboideae.
cards.keyFeatures: Dipogon lignosus is climbing woody, herbaceous perennial which becomes woody towards the base. The soft green stems climb over nearby structures, shrubs or trees, and can grow up to 2 m tall, extending a long way horizontally if possible.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nicola van Berkel, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Nicola van Berkel

cards.name: Smooth Riceflower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea glauca
cards.description: Pimelea glauca, commonly known as smooth riceflower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It has elliptic to more or less lance-shaped or linear leaves and creamy-white flowers arranged in heads of seven or more on the ends of the stems, with four lance-shaped to egg-shaped bracts at the base of the inflorescence.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea glauca is a much-branched shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in) and has glabrous stems. The leaves are narrowly elliptic to lance-shaped or linear, 3–15 mm (0.12–0.59 in) long and 1–6 mm (0.039–0.236 in) wide ending with a short, downward curving, sharp point.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Mountain Silkpod
cards.subtitle: Parsonsia brownii
cards.description: Parsonsia brownii, commonly known as twining silkpod or mountain silkpod, is a woody vine of the dogbane family, Apocynaceae. It occurs in rainforest in the states of New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania in Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The species climbs to 10 or more metres in height and has a watery sap. The glossy leaves are lanceolate, up to 20 centimetres long and 4 centimetres wide, and taper towards the tip.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bryce Watts-Parker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bryce Watts-Parker

cards.name: Silky Guinea-flower
cards.subtitle: Hibbertia sericea
cards.description: Hibbertia sericea, commonly known as silky guinea-flower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Dilleniaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect or spreading shrub with softly-hairy branches, elliptic to egg-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, and yellow flowers with eight to fourteen stamens in a cluster on one side of two hairy carpels.
cards.keyFeatures: Hibbertia sericea is a erect or spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 30–70 cm (12–28 in) with softly-hairy young branches. The leaves are elliptic to egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, 1.8–22 mm (0.071–0.866 in) long, 0.9–5.1 mm (0.035–0.201 in) wide and woolly-hairy on the lower surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) T. Hammer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by T. Hammer

cards.name: Madeira Vine
cards.subtitle: Anredera cordifolia
cards.description: Anredera cordifolia, commonly known as the Madeira vine or mignonette vine, is a South American species of ornamental succulent vine of the family Basellaceae. The combination of fleshy leaves and thick aerial tubers makes this a very heavy vine. It smothers trees and other vegetation it grows on and can easily break branches and bring down entire trees on its own.
cards.keyFeatures: Anredera cordifolia is an evergreen climber that grows from fleshy rhizomes. It has bright green, heart-shaped, fleshy shiny leaves 4–13 centimetres (1.6–5.1 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Allen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: River Rose
cards.subtitle: Bauera rubioides
cards.description: Bauera rubioides, commonly known as river rose, dog rose or wiry bauera, is a species of flowering plant in the family Cunoniaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a scrambling, tangled shrub with wiry branches, trifoliate, usually toothed leaves, and pink or white flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Bauera rubioides is a scrambling, tangled shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 2 m (6 ft 7 in) and has wiry, extensively-branched stems. The leaves are trifoliate, the leaflets narrowly elliptic, mostly 3–15 mm (0.12–0.59 in) long, 1.5–5.0 mm (0.059–0.197 in) wide and usually have four to ten teeth on each edge.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Zara, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Thin-leaf Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia aculeatissima
cards.description: Acacia aculeatissima, commonly known as thin-leaf wattle or snake wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is usually a prostrate shrub with sharply pointed, needle-shaped phyllodes, flowers arranged in up to 3 more or less spherical heads of 15 to 25 flowers, and linear, papery pods up to 60 mm (2.4 in) long.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia aculeatissima is an open, prostrate shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 50 cm (20 in), rarely to 1 m (3 ft 3 in) and has finely ribbed, hairy branchlets. Its phyllodes are needle-shaped, curved backwards, 5–12 mm (0.20–0.47 in) long and 0.5–1 mm (0.020–0.039 in) wide and sharply pointed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Ploughshare Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia gunnii
cards.description: Acacia gunnii, commonly known as ploughshare wattle or dog's tooth wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia gunnii is a diffuse, prostrate or erect shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in) and usually has hairy branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) grampianshiker, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Apple Berry
cards.subtitle: Billardiera scandens
cards.description: Billardiera scandens, commonly known as hairy apple berry or common apple-berry, is a small shrub or twining plant of the Pittosporaceae family which occurs in forests in the coastal and tableland areas of all states and territories in Australia, apart from the Northern Territory and Western Australia. It has a silky touch and appearance that becomes more brittle as the dense growth matures.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Creeping Myoporum
cards.subtitle: Myoporum parvifolium
cards.description: Myoporum parvifolium, commonly known as creeping boobialla, creeping myoporum, dwarf native myrtle or small leaved myoporum is a plant in the figwort family, Scrophulariaceae. It is a low, spreading shrub with long, trailing stems and white, star-shaped flowers and is endemic to southern Australia including Flinders Island.
cards.keyFeatures: Creeping boobialla is a prostrate, spreading shrub sometimes forming a mat 3 metres (10 ft) in diameter. Its leaves are fleshy and glabrous, usually 18–40 millimetres (0.7–2 in) long, 3–6.5 millimetres (0.1–0.3 in) wide and egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Irene

cards.name: Holly Lomatia
cards.subtitle: Lomatia ilicifolia
cards.description: Lomatia ilicifolia, commonly known as holly lomatia or native holly, is a plant in the family Proteaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a stiff, erect shrub with hairy, rust-coloured new growth and which recovers from fire from a lignotuber. It has dull green, leathery, prickly, holly-like leaves and long sprays of cream flowers, usually after fire.
cards.keyFeatures: Lomatia ilicifolia is a stiff, erect shrub which grows to a height of 0.5–3 m (2–10 ft) and has its young foliage and flower buds covered with rust-coloured hairs. The leaves are dull green, leathery and holly-like, mostly glabrous and egg-shaped to lance-shaped or elliptic.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Beaded Samphire
cards.subtitle: Salicornia quinqueflora
cards.description: Salicornia quinqueflora, synonym Sarcocornia quinqueflora, commonly known as beaded samphire, bead weed, beaded glasswort or glasswort, is a species of succulent halophytic coastal shrub. It occurs in wetter coastal areas of Australia and New Zealand. Historically, people used to burn glassworts to collect the ashes.
cards.keyFeatures: Beaded glasswort, Salicornia quinqueflora, is a species of succulent, salt tolerant plant. It grows as a small shrub, with a lifecycle of several years – which is also known as a perennial lifecycle.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacob Moore, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Jacob Moore

cards.name: Downy Dodder-laurel
cards.subtitle: Cassytha pubescens
cards.description: Cassytha pubescens is a native Australian hemiparasitic vine species, in the Laurel family. Common names for the species include devils twine, dodder-laurel, spilled devil's twine, snotty gobble or downy dodder-laurel. It is a widespread and common species in south eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Cassytha pubescens grows as a photosynthetic stem that twines around itself and around the branches of its host. Stems are between 0.5 and 1.5 mm thick and can be highly variable in appearance.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Dylan Wishart, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Flinders Range Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia iteaphylla
cards.description: Acacia iteaphylla, commonly known as Flinders Range wattle, Port Lincoln wattle, winter wattle or willow-leaved wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to South Australia, but has become naturalised as an environmental weed outside of its natural range.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia iteaphylla is a bushy, spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of 2–4 m (6 ft 7 in – 13 ft 1 in) and has greenish bark on young plants. Its branchlets are glabrous, often become pendulous, and are usually covered with a thin, whitish powdery bloom.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Leonora Enking, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA)

cards.name: Large-leaf Eutaxia
cards.subtitle: Eutaxia diffusa
cards.description: Eutaxia diffusa, commonly known as spreading eutaxia, is a shrub species in the family Fabaceae. The species is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants grow to between 0.5 and 1 metre high with a similar spread. The small, grey green, obovate (or narrow obovate) leaves are lighter coloured beneath and have an acute tip.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jacob Moore, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Rusty Bush-pea
cards.subtitle: Pultenaea hispidula
cards.description: Pultenaea hispidula, commonly known as rusty bush-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is an erect, spreading shrub with many drooping branches, oblong to egg-shaped leaves with the narrower end towards the base, and yellow to pale orange and red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pultenaea hispidula is an erect, spreading shrub with many drooping, densely hairy branches and that typically grows to a height of about 1 m (3 ft 3 in).
cards.imageCredit: (c) Max Campbell, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Max Campbell

cards.name: Rambling Dock
cards.subtitle: Rumex sagittatus
cards.description: Rumex sagittatus, synonym Acetosa sagittata, commonly known as turkey rhubarb or rambling dock or potato vine, is a herbaceous perennial plant native to southern Africa, which has become a weed in Australia and New Zealand.
cards.keyFeatures: Rumex sagittatus is a soft-stemmed herbaceous scrambling and climbing plant with prominent triangular arrow-shaped leaves 3–6 cm (1.2–2.4 in) in length and 2–4 cm (0.8–1.6 in) wide. The grooved green stem may be distinctly tinted red at times.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Large-leaf Cotoneaster
cards.subtitle: Cotoneaster glaucophyllus
cards.description: Cotoneaster glaucophyllus, commonly known as glaucous cotoneaster' or bright bead cotoneaster, is a native plant of China and the Himalayas. Cotoneaster glaucophyllus is a spreading evergreen shrub growing up to 5 metres (16 ft) tall. The oblong leaves are 1.5–4 centimetres (0.59–1.57 in) wide by 3–8 centimetres (1.2–3.1 in) long, with hairy undersides when young.
cards.keyFeatures: The plant is 4 metres (13 ft) tall with arched and erect branches which are greenish to purple-black in colour. Fertile shoots are 40–70 millimetres (1.6–2.8 in) long including two to four leaves.
cards.imageCredit: (c) sblumen, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Rosy Heath-myrtle
cards.subtitle: Euryomyrtus ramosissima
cards.description: Euryomyrtus ramosissima, the rosy baeckea, is a shrub in the myrtle family (Myrtaceae). The species is endemic to Australia. It is spreading in habit and grows to 60 cm in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Peter Crowcroft

cards.name: Common Eutaxia
cards.subtitle: Eutaxia microphylla
cards.description: Eutaxia microphylla, also known as common eutaxia, is a shrub species in the family Fabaceae. The species is endemic to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Plants grow to between 30 and 40 centimetres high. The small, grey green, narrow to ovate leaves are 2.3 to 4 mm long and 0.6 to 0.9 mm wide.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Andrew Thornhill, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Andrew Thornhill

cards.name: Globe-pea
cards.subtitle: Sphaerolobium minus
cards.description: Sphaerolobium minus, commonly known as globe-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is an erect, rush-like, mostly leafless shrub with yellow and reddish flowers arranged in small groups along the stems.
cards.keyFeatures: Sphaerolobium minus is an erect, rush-like shrub that typically grows to a height of up to about 50 cm (20 in) and has glabrous branchlets. It is mostly leafless, but when present, the leaves are scattered, linear to lance-shaped and about 5 mm (0.20 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) T. Hammer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by T. Hammer

cards.name: Sweet-brier
cards.subtitle: Rosa rubiginosa
cards.description: Rosa rubiginosa (sweet briar, sweetbriar rose, sweet brier or eglantine; syn. R. eglanteria) is a species of rose native to Europe and western Asia.
cards.keyFeatures: It is a dense deciduous shrub 2–3 meters (6.6–9.8 ft) high and across, with the stems bearing numerously hooked prickles. The foliage has a strong apple-like fragrance.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Marco Mussita, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Marco Mussita

cards.name: Blue Star Creeper
cards.subtitle: Isotoma fluviatilis
cards.description: Isotoma fluviatilis, the swamp isotome or blue star creeper, is a small herbaceous perennial plant in the family Campanulaceae, native to Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: This plant often forms a low growing mat. It is usually pubescent or sometimes glabrous and roots at nodes.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Gorse Bitter Pea
cards.subtitle: Daviesia ulicifolia
cards.description: Daviesia ulicifolia, commonly known as gorse bitter-pea, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a rigid, openly-branched shrub with sharply-pointed, narrow elliptic, narrow egg-shaped, rarely egg-shaped phyllodes and usually orange-yellow and dark red flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Daviesia ulicifolia is a rigid, openly-branched shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 2.5 m (8 ft 2 in) and has spiny branchlets. Its phyllodes are narrow elliptic, narrow egg-shaped, rarely egg-shaped, 5–35 mm (0.20–1.38 in) long and 0.5–6 mm (0.020–0.236 in) wide and sharply pointed with a prominent midrib on the upper surface.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Harry Rose, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Star-bush
cards.subtitle: Asterolasia asteriscophora
cards.description: Asterolasia asteriscophora, commonly known as lemon starbush, is a species of slender, erect shrub in the family Rutaceae and is endemic to southern continental Australia. It has woolly, star-shaped hairs on its young branches, variably-shaped leaves covered with brownish or whitish hairs on the underside, and yellow flowers with brown, star-shaped hairs on the back.
cards.keyFeatures: Asterolasia asteriscophora is a slender, erect shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) with its young branches covered with woolly, grey to brown star-shaped hairs. The leaves are spatula-shaped, egg-shaped, wedge-shaped or elliptic, 3–30 mm (0.12–1.18 in) long and 2–10 mm (0.079–0.394 in) wide on a short petiole.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Sticky Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia howittii
cards.description: Acacia howittii, commonly known as sticky wattle or Howitt's wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to Victoria, Australia. It is a graceful shrub or small tree with pendulous branchlets, narrowly elliptic to lance-shaped phyllodes, spherical heads of pale lemon yellow flowers and narrowly oblong to linear, firmly papery to thinly leathery pods.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia howittii is a graceful shrub or three that typically grows to a height of up to 9 m (30 ft) and it has slender, pendulous branchlets with hairy ribs. Its phyllodes are narrowly elliptic to lance-shaped, usually 15–25 mm (0.59–0.98 in) long, 4–8 mm (0.16–0.31 in) wide, dark green and glabrous with two or three veins on each face.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Melburnian, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Horny Cone-bush
cards.subtitle: Isopogon ceratophyllus
cards.description: Isopogon ceratophyllus, commonly known as the horny cone-bush or wild Irishman, is a plant of the family Proteaceae that is endemic to the coast in Victoria, South Australia and on the Furneaux Group of islands in Tasmania. It is a small woody shrub that grows to 100 cm (40 in) high with prickly foliage. It is extremely sensitive to dieback from the pathogen Phytophthora cinnamomi
cards.keyFeatures: Isopogon ceratophyllus is a prickly shrub, growing to 15–100 cm (6–40 in) tall and to 120 cm (4 ft) across. The oval to round flower heads, known as inflorescences, appear between July and January, and are around 3 cm in diameter.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Connor Margetts, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Connor Margetts

cards.name: Coast Everlasting
cards.subtitle: Ozothamnus turbinatus
cards.description: Ozothamnus turbinatus, the coast everlasting, is a shrub in the family Asteraceae, native to the states of New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia and Tasmania in Australia. It grows to between 1 and 2 metres in height.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Saira Manns, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Woolly Wattle
cards.subtitle: Acacia lanigera
cards.description: Acacia lanigera, commonly known as woolly wattle or hairy wattle, is a species of flowering plant in the family Fabaceae and is endemic to the south-east of continental Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: Acacia lanigera is a rigid shrub that typically grows to a height of 1–2 m (3 ft 3 in – 6 ft 7 in) and has hairy branchlets.
cards.imageCredit: (c) ttsquid, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Bearded Heath
cards.subtitle: Styphelia ericoides
cards.description: Styphelia ericoides, commonly known as the pink beard-heath, is a species of flowering plant in the heath family Ericaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a slender shrub with oblong leaves, and white to pinkish, tube-shaped flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Styphelia ericoides is a slender shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.3–2 m (1 ft 0 in – 6 ft 7 in), its branchlets softly hairy.
cards.imageCredit: (c) James (Jim) Duggan, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by James (Jim) Duggan

cards.name: Forked Rice-flower
cards.subtitle: Pimelea hewardiana
cards.description: Pimelea hewardiana, commonly known as forked rice-flower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Thymelaeaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is a shrub with narrowly elliptic leaves and head-like clusters of 7 to 34 unisexual yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pimelea hewardiana is a shrub that typically grows to a height of 40–70 cm (16–28 in), it young stems covered with short hairs. The leaves are arranged in opposite pairs, narrowly elliptic to egg-shaped with the narrower end towards the base, 3–11.5 mm (0.12–0.45 in) long, 1.0–3.5 mm (0.039–0.138 in) wide on a short petiole.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Nina Kerr, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Nina Kerr

cards.name: Prickly Geebung
cards.subtitle: Persoonia juniperina
cards.description: Persoonia juniperina, commonly known as prickly geebung, is a species of flowering plant in the family Proteaceae and is endemic to south-eastern Australia. It is a small erect to low-lying shrub with smooth bark, hairy new branches, linear leaves, yellow flowers borne singly or in groups of up to forty in leaf axils, and yellowish green to purplish fruit.
cards.keyFeatures: Persoonia juniperina is an erect to low-lying shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.3–2 m (1 ft 0 in – 6 ft 7 in) with smooth bark and hairy young branchlets. The leaves are linear, 8–35 mm (0.31–1.38 in) long and 0.7–1.5 mm (0.028–0.059 in) wide.
cards.imageCredit: no rights reserved, uploaded by Cowirrie

cards.name: Coastal Rosemary
cards.subtitle: Westringia fruticosa
cards.description: Westringia fruticosa, the coastal rosemary or coastal westringia, is a shrub that grows near the coast in eastern Australia.
cards.keyFeatures: The flowers are white, hairy and have the upper petal divided into two lobes. They also have orange-to-purply spots on their bottom half.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Bryce Watts-Parker, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Bryce Watts-Parker

cards.name: Prickly Broom-heath
cards.subtitle: Monotoca scoparia
cards.description: Monotoca scoparia, commonly known as prickly broom heath, is a widespread native species across south-eastern Australia. Monotoca scoparia was formerly in the family Epacridaceae but now belongs to the family Ericaceae. Monotoca is an endemic Australian genus with 17 described species occurring in all states.
cards.keyFeatures: Monotoca scoparia is a lignotuberous shrub that grows usually between 30–120 cm high. The alternating leaves are erect and prickly, and narrowly oblong to elliptic in shape.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Petra Holland, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Petra Holland

cards.name: Trailing Ground-berry
cards.subtitle: Acrotriche prostrata
cards.description: Acrotriche prostrata, commonly known as trailing ground-berry, is a species of flowering plant in the family Ericaceae and is endemic to Victoria. It is a trailing shrub with prostrate stems, widely spreading, lance-shaped to egg-shaped leaves and spikes of 5 to 14 light green flowers and spherical, green drupes.
cards.keyFeatures: Acrotriche prostrata is a training shrub that has prostrate main stems and short side stems that sometimes grow to a height of up to about 15 cm (5.9 in), the branchlets hairy. The leaves are widely-spreading, lance-shaped to egg-shaped, 4–16 mm (0.16–0.63 in) long, 1–8 mm (0.039–0.315 in) wide and sharply-pointed.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Elspeth Swan, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Elspeth Swan

cards.name: Turkeybush
cards.subtitle: Eremophila deserti
cards.description: Eremophila deserti is a shrub which is endemic to Australia. Common names for this species include turkey bush, dogwood, poison bush Ellangowan poison bush, pencil bush and carrot bush. It is common and widespread in all mainland states, although not the Northern Territory.
cards.keyFeatures: Eremophila deserti varies in habit from a low spreading shrub 0.5 m (2 ft) high to a tall erect shrub up to 4 m (10 ft) high. Its leaves and branches are sticky and shiny when young due to the presence of resin.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Kym Nicolson, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Kym Nicolson

cards.name: Sea Heath
cards.subtitle: Frankenia pauciflora
cards.description: Frankenia pauciflora, the common sea-heath or southern sea-heath, is an evergreen shrub native to southern Australia. It is part of the Frankenia genus of the Frankeniaceae family. It can be prostrate or may grow up to 0.5 m in height.
cards.keyFeatures: Individuals of this species are prostrate perennial shrubs up to 0.5 m in height. It forms many branches that create a thick mat-like structure.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Peter Crowcroft, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Peter Crowcroft

cards.name: Black Roly-poly
cards.subtitle: Sclerolaena muricata
cards.description: Sclerolaena muricata, commonly known as black rolypoly, is a perennial shrub native to eastern and central Australia.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Russell Best, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Russell Best

cards.name: Woolly Pomaderris
cards.subtitle: Pomaderris lanigera
cards.description: Pomaderris lanigera, commonly known as woolly pomaderris, is a species of flowering plant in the family Rhamnaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is a shrub or small tree with hairy stems, lance-shaped to egg-shaped or elliptic leaves, and hemispherical clusters of yellow flowers.
cards.keyFeatures: Pomaderris lanigera is a shrub that typically grows to a height of 0.5–3 m (1 ft 8 in – 9 ft 10 in), its branchlets covered with shaggy, rust-coloured and star-shaped hairs.
cards.imageCredit: (c) prossington, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Sea Box
cards.subtitle: Alyxia buxifolia
cards.description: Alyxia buxifolia, otherwise known as the sea box or dysentery bush, is a species of evergreen shrub in the family Apocynaceae. Alyxia buxifolia has medium to dark green foliage consisting of small, fleshy leaves. The flowers are small and twisted anticlockwise in a star shape.
cards.keyFeatures: Alyxia buxifolia is a dense, woody shrub that can grow to 3 metres high and 3 metres wide. However, it is often found to be less than 50 cm tall due to harsh winds in it natural coastal habitats.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Tim, some rights reserved (CC BY-SA), uploaded by Tim

cards.name: Erect Guinea-flower
cards.subtitle: Hibbertia australis
cards.description: Hibbertia australis is a species of flowering plant in the family Dilleniaceae and is endemic to south-eastern continental Australia. It is an erect to spreading shrub with linear leaves and yellow flowers with four to nine stamens arranged in a single cluster.
cards.keyFeatures: Hibbertia australis is an erect to spreading shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 60 cm (24 in), the young branchlets with star-shaped hairs. The leaves are linear, 4–16 mm (0.16–0.63 in) long and 1–2 mm (0.039–0.079 in) wide and sessile or on a petiole up to 0.7 mm (0.028 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) T. Hammer, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by T. Hammer

cards.name: Himalayan Honeysuckle
cards.subtitle: Leycesteria formosa
cards.description: Leycesteria formosa, the pheasant berry, is a deciduous shrub in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to the Himalayas and southwestern China. It is considered a noxious invasive species in Australia, New Zealand, the neighbouring islands of Micronesia, and some other places. In the Himalayas, the shrub is frequently used in the traditional medicine of the various countries and peoples encompassed within the region.
cards.keyFeatures: It is found to be a hardy evergreen, requiring a considerable degree of moisture, and a situation slightly sheltered and shaded, though the colour of its bracts would be most probably be heightened by exposure to solar light.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Jon Sullivan, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Prickly Guinea Flower
cards.subtitle: Hibbertia acicularis
cards.description: Hibbertia acicularis, commonly known as prickly guinea-flower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Dilleniaceae and is endemic to eastern Australia. It is an erect or prostrate shrub with linear to lance-shaped leaves and yellow flowers arranged singly in leaf axils with the six to eight stamens joined at the base, in a single cluster.
cards.keyFeatures: Hibbertia acicularis is an erect to prostrate, openly-branched shrub that typically grows to a height of up to 1 m (3 ft 3 in). The leaves are linear to lance-shaped with an awned tip, mostly 7–9 mm (0.28–0.35 in) long and 0.6–0.7 mm (0.024–0.028 in) wide on a petiole 0.2–0.5 mm (0.0079–0.0197 in) long.
cards.imageCredit: (c) John Tann, some rights reserved (CC BY)

cards.name: Heavenly Bamboo
cards.subtitle: Nandina domestica
cards.description: Nandina domestica ( nan-DEE-nə) commonly known as nandina, heavenly bamboo or sacred bamboo, is a species of flowering plant in the family Berberidaceae, native to eastern Asia from the Himalayas to Japan. It is the only member of the monotypic genus Nandina. Despite its name, it is not a true bamboo.
cards.keyFeatures: Despite the common name "sacred bamboo", it is not a bamboo but an erect evergreen shrub up to 2 m (7 ft) tall by 1.5 m (5 ft) wide, with numerous, usually unbranched stems growing from ground level.
cards.imageCredit: (c) Sam Kieschnick, some rights reserved (CC BY), uploaded by Sam Kieschnick

cards.name: Cape Honeysuckle
cards.subtitle: Tecomaria capensis
